findings.where: Until Loop argument: 'Work: Implement step {{step_id}} of work item {{item_id}} by the Method in {{packet_abs}} ...', the four Exit lines and 'Repeat while an exit condition is unmet and a justified fix remains ...'
findings.evidence: Compared with RUN/loops/nav-2a6055a02c0845838f348ae058d7d65d-contract.json: work 406 vs 614 characters, exit 498 vs 539, repeat 295 vs 673; all three differ. The contract comes from shiploop_loops.WORK_STEP, REPEAT_STEP and stage_spec STEP_CRITERIA_CONDITION/STEP_PROOF_CONDITION, and check_loop_packet compares the receipt with that rebuilt contract. No refusal follows, but the runtime prints the contract's text in every loop packet, so the model is judged by an argument the ShipLoop packet does not show. The Improve hand-off also quotes worded_stage().done_when, so a third copy would drift.

Move any new wording into WORK_STEP, REPEAT_STEP and the stage_spec constants in the same commit, and add a test that the printed argument equals the contract file.

findings.where: Method 5: 'Report revise ... Report blocked only when a person, an access grant or an outside dependency must resolve it.' vs argument: 'Stop blocked and report revise, ... when no justified next action remains or Method 5 applies.'
findings.evidence: The Repeat sends every Method 5 case to revise, but Method 5's last sentence sends person, access and outside cases to blocked. 'Stop blocked' is a loop stop (continuation_assessment blocked, until_loop_ephemeral._transition -> status stopped), while 'report blocked' is a result outcome. That is the vocabulary mix the brief names. check_loop_packet accepts both outcomes from a stopped receipt, so the rule decides, and it is stated twice in conflict. The RULES partial gives a third wording ('only when nothing can proceed without a person').
findings.fix: Repeat (in WORK_STEP/REPEAT_STEP's home): 'Stop the loop (continuation_assessment blocked) when no justified next action remains or Method 5 applies; then report the outcome Method 5 names.' Method 5 keeps the only wording of when revise vs blocked applies.

findings.where: loop-result: 'If the Callback refuses for the loop, run the receipt's next_argv once, then the Callback again.'; loop-invoke resume branch: 'do not start it again (a second start resets it)'
findings.evidence: check_loop_packet requires a terminal receipt to have next_argv None, so on a complete or stopped receipt that the gate rejects (contract mismatch, stopped plus done, cancelled), the only route printed does not exist. Those refusals, and _step_proof_gate's refusal ('Start the Until Loop again with: <start> (it replaces the receipt)'), tell the model to restart, while the resume branch forbids it. Today's RESULT_LINE kept 'run the start command above again (an active receipt: its next_argv instead)'. This is partial-owned but breaks implement's refusal routes.
findings.fix: loop-result: 'If the Callback refuses for the loop: with an active receipt, run its next_argv once; with a complete or stopped receipt, start the loop again with the command the refusal prints; then run the Callback again.' Resume branch: 'do not start it again while it is active (a second start resets it)'.

Highest-risk spot; live runs always expanded it (no RUN/ or HOME/ directory in the Battleship worktree, no literal symbol path in any implement CALL).
Method 1 'a one-line probe in RUN/scratch': RUN can read as the verb ('run ... in scratch'), and the path can be copied into a shell command.

Case rows '(procedure: HOME/architecture.md ## Procedures ### fleet)' and Anchors 'HOME/spec.md', 'HOME/architecture.md ## Decisions', 'HOME/environment.md ## Commands': HOME reads as $HOME (~/architecture.md).

Argument 'Contract: RUN/loops/...' / 'Receipt: RUN/loops/...-terminal.json': today these lines are absolute. A model that reads or cats the Receipt by this line gets a relative path. evidence_refs would still expand it (expand_result_roots).

Methods 4-5 'R-<n>', 'AD-<n>' sit beside result-rules' 'every placeholder (<...>) replaced'. '<n>' looks like a fill-in, the same angle-bracket syntax as the form's placeholders, and test-spec's HANDOFF placeholder 'R-<n>' is refused when unfilled.
Frame 'HOME = WORKTREE/docs/shiploop' defines one symbol through another, so a reader must expand twice.

verdict.summary: The implement template is a real gain on the live packet. It fits under the Grok cut (18,793 printed against 21,600 bytes live, which lost the middle), prints the Proof with its directory (fixing S1's failed first run), quotes only this step's R-<n>, keys the revisit to the step (fixing today's S1 revisit that cited S4's result), and cuts Code craft to one line per rule. But it is not yet the gate's contract. Its result form adds criterion_evidence, which today's _canonical_result refuses as an unsupported field while its own exit 4 demands it (P0). Its loop argument is literal text that differs from the contract ShipLoop writes and compares in all three lines. The S4 Proof (1,036 characters) is over the 'refuse' bound with no producer gate (P0 render stall). Its placeholders, outcome names and not_covered shape do not come from the gate's tables, so the frame's 'states every rule its gates apply' fails for nine refusals. On the owner's N2 asks it keeps the problem: there is no commit look-back, no step commit line and no learned/decisions keys, although 0 of 8 live implement steps read the history that 7 of 8 Improve reviews used. One step at a time is mostly honoured. Later steps print by first sentence (needed by exit 1, against N2's 'count only'), and the item's other requirements and the item's case list are not shown, so 'none broken' and not_covered cannot be judged from the print.
top_changes: Generate the variable parts from the code tables the gates read: the loop argument from loops.contract(...); outcomes from stage_spec; placeholders, not_covered and lint_waivers shapes from HEADLINE_PLACEHOLDER, guidance.summary_placeholder and HANDOFF_SHAPES; drop criterion_evidence (and exit 4's mention) until its gate is on main; then route-test the unfilled and filled forms through the real complete.

Add N2: a commit look-back slot (last two non-bookkeeping commits from the step's starting HEAD, plus the step's own previous commit on a revisit), short commits on accepted-step rows, learned/decisions keys, and 'ShipLoop commits this step; commit nothing yourself' in the head.

Make bounds and the completeness claims true: adopt the T-D2 producer bounds with step-plan refusals before any 'refuse' slot policy; replace 'they are complete for this step' with 'excerpts: open each named section'; print the item's case IDs and the test-spec locator for not_covered, and replace the Battleship-only '## Procedures' locator with case fields.
